desc: Derive & document the formula: for center `c`, with neighbor values `a = deg(m)-1` sorted descending, best kept size is `max_{i: a_i≥1} (1 + i*(a_i+1))`; answer = `N - global max`.
Implement the full NumPy solution (fast parsing + vectorized lexsort/rank/max) and hand-verify against the three samples (traced: 8→1, 3→0, 10→3, all match).

Edge cases & finalize: N=3 path (center must be an endpoint; the `w>=1` mask correctly excludes the middle vertex), all-leaf-neighbor centers (`a=0`) masked, empty-mask guard `best=3`, 1-indexed `bincount(minlength=N+1)`, int64 arithmetic (values ≤ N, no overflow).

Correctness argument that no matching/conflict handling is needed: in a tree, two middles adjacent to the center cannot be adjacent, and leaf sets of distinct middles are disjoint (any overlap or extra edge would create a cycle), so the kept set induces exactly a snowflake.
Complexity/performance check: O(N log N) via a single lexsort over 2(N−1) directed edges plus `searchsorted` for group starts; buffered stdin parsing; no recursion — safe at N = 3·10⁵.
